findings.title: formIsInvariant throws RangeError 'is not an integer' on an integer form entry beyond 2^53, so the Gram matrix of a board with such a road count cannot be tested, where form_is_invariant answers
findings.claim: fromAdjacency accepts road counts beyond 2^53, and since the fix of P4-RT-01-02 gram returns their exact Gram matrix. formIsInvariant refuses that matrix, whose integer entries are exact doubles, with a RangeError naming them non-integers. The oracle answers True for the Gram matrix and False for a changed one.
findings.expected: C = [[2,-2^53],[-1,2]] (fromAdjacency, Big): form_is_invariant(C, [[2,-2^53],[-2^53,2^54]]) = True, and = False for [[4,-2^53],[-2^53,2^54]] (witness (0, (0, 1))). C = [[2,-2^60],[-2,2]]: form_is_invariant(C, gram(C)) = True. decisions/P2-A1.md allows a RangeError only for a form matrix that is 'not integer'.
findings.observed: formIsInvariant(board, M) throws 'RangeError: the form entry at (0, 1) is not an integer' for the entry -9007199254740992 (= -2^53). It does so for gram(C) of all 5 boards with road counts 2^53, 2^54 and 2^60 in redteam-RT-01-diff-huge-siblings.test.ts, and in 3 of 4 tests of the reproducer (the test that gram itself is exact passes). With Number.isInteger in place of Number.isSafeInteger at form.ts:104 (applied temporarily and reverted), the reproducer passes 4 of 4.
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of 006f50d plus the reproducer: npm ci --prefer-offline; npx vitest run --root packages/engine packages/engine/test/unit/redteam-RT-01-p5-01-form-invariant-beyond-2-53.test.ts (3 failed, 1 passed; no Python needed, the oracle values are typed in)
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 5.4 table, formIsInvariant ('does every mutation preserve the form with matrix M?', oracle form_is_invariant); 5.6 first table (a road count may be any integer) and second table (formIsInvariant works off the finite types); E-2 (every other board uses Big); decisions/P2-A1.md (RangeError for a form matrix 'not integer'); RT-01 attack 25 (gram(C) itself among the inputs); sibling of P4-RT-01-02 (decisions/RT-FIX-P4-engine.md: only symmetrizer and gram were moved to bigint).
findings.proposedFix: In checkSymmetricMatrix accept any integer number (Number.isInteger) and convert it with BigInt(x), which is exact for every integer double; keep RangeError for non-integers and non-symmetric matrices.

notes: Incidental, for RT-05 and RT-08 (wording). T12 prints 'Dimension: N' (data-out=dimension, T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:1079) for every node, and dimensionOf falls back to the orbit size. On a node that is not minuscule this number is the size of the orbit and of the matrices, not the dimension of the representation with highest weight omega_i. Oracle weyl_dimension against T12: D4 node 2, 28 against 24; F4 node 4, 26 against 24; E8 node 8, 248 against 240. On E8 node 1 the tool shows 2160 (not built), while V(omega_1) has dimension 3875 (standard value, not computed here). M8 beat 6 states 248 for E8 on the same site. SPEC 4 T12 defines no dimension fact for these nodes, and the number is the engine's correct orbitSize, so this is not filed as an RT-01 finding. The P5-A3 review raised the F4 case.

For RT-03 and RT-10 (SafeInt on its own terms). SafeInt throws EngineOverflow on an intermediate product even when the input and the result are safe. fire(boardFromName('A3'), [2^52, 1, 0], 0) throws 'mul gave 9007199254740992' because the diagonal term C_ii a_i = 2a_i is checked; Big gives (-2^52, 2^52+1, 0), as the oracle does. wythoffEdges(A3, [2^52+1, 0, 1]) on SafeInt throws while every edge entry is safe, because its compare subtracts two entries. E-2 says SafeInt checks 'every result', so this is the documented behaviour, and tools that reload with Big on EngineOverflow are unaffected. T12's fireText and stringView do so, verified on starts near 2^53.
